- Latency targets: P95 ~100-120ms (US/EU), P95 ~150-180ms (APAC) for user-facing flows.
- Throughput: baseline 5k reqs/min across regions; expected peak bursts ~12k reqs/min.
- Concurrency: ~200-300 concurrent inference requests during peak.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for chat flows (SSE/WebSocket acceptable).
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU; US data in US. APAC to prefer Singapore region.

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Region splits (approx): US 55%, EU 30%, APAC 15% (APAC expected to grow rapidly).
- Latency: P95 targets above are correct as our goal — US/EU 100-120ms, APAC up to 180ms tolerable for now.
- Concurrency: we expect short bursts up to ~300 concurrent inference requests during heavy customer events.
- Streaming: yes, token-level streaming (SSE) for chat is mandatory for our product UX.
- Data residency: must keep EU-originated customer data and associated logs within EU data centers. Same for US; cross-region replication is allowable only with customer consent.

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear targets. Sharing a technical summary and preliminary recommendations below; we can walk through these in the deep-dive.

Short answers to your asks: 
- Regional residency: Yes — we can provision region-scoped deployments (hosted or Dedicated) with logs and KMS keys anchored to the same region. EU data can be restricted to EU regions (and not replicated) by default; cross-region replication is opt-in.
- Failover vs residency: We recommend a primary-region-first routing policy for residency requirements (requests originating in EU served by EU pools). Failover to other regions for availability is supported but must be explicitly enabled per customer; doing so may have residency tradeoffs we’ll document.
- Audit logs / KMS: Per-region KMS integration and region-retained audit logs are supported on Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API can be configured for regional log retention for enterprise accounts.

Performance & architecture recommendations: 
- Deployment: Regional Dedicated pools (US / EU / APAC-SG) to meet steady-state throughput and hit P95 targets. If you want lower commit, a hybrid model (regional hosted + Dedicated in EU) can be used for residency-sensitive traffic.
- Model sizing & quantization: For conversational workloads we typically recommend a quantized 13B variant (int8/awq) for best latency/throughput balance. On RTX A100/RTX 6000-type hardware we expect P95 ~80-110ms for 13B under continuous batching for typical prompt lengths (<=256 tokens).
- Throughput & concurrency: Target per-region concurrency pool sizing ~300-400 slots to handle bursts + warmup. Continuous batching will help amortize cost; configure max_batch_delay ~12-20ms to preserve P95.
- Streaming: We support chunked SSE and WebSocket streaming. Ensure keepalive and small chunk sizes on the client to reduce perceived latency. We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated context to reduce token compute.
- Routing: Use smart routing by geo-IP + user tenancy. For EU residency, mark EU tenants and route to EU pools; set fallback policy to fail rather than cross-region serve unless explicitly permitted.
- Testing plan: We’ll run a soak + stress test: 30-minute ramp to expected peak, 10-minute sustained peak, and 15-minute spike to 1.5x. We’ll measure P50/P95/P99 and error rates.

Attachments: architecture diagram + a short SLO proposal PDF with numeric assumptions (attached). I’ve also added a small note on streaming behavior and client tuning.

If this aligns, Marissa — I’ll schedule the deep-dive and we can include an ops person to walk through KMS/audit log proofs.
